Stage 1: Foundations
1. Programming & Tools

Python:

Variables, data types, type conversion

Lists, tuples, dictionaries, sets

Loops (for, while), conditionals (if-else)

Functions (def, lambda), scope

List comprehensions

Exception handling (try-except)

Object-Oriented Programming (OOP): Classes, Inheritance, Encapsulation

Time & datetime module usage


Libraries & Tools:

NumPy: arrays, broadcasting, indexing

Pandas: Series, DataFrames, indexing, GroupBy, aggregation, datetime

Matplotlib & Seaborn: basic & advanced plotting

Scikit-learn: model building, evaluation, pipelines

Jupyter Notebook: writing clean, interactive code

Git & GitHub: version control

Linux Basics: CLI commands, file system, bash


Stage 2: Mathematics

Statistics:

Mean, median, mode, variance, standard deviation

Probability basics, permutations & combinations

Distributions: Normal, Binomial, Poisson

Conditional Probability, Bayes' Theorem


Linear Algebra:

Scalars, vectors, matrices

Matrix operations (dot product, transpose, inverse)

Eigenvalues and eigenvectors


Calculus:

Derivatives and gradients

Cost function and optimization intuition


Probability Theory:

Joint, marginal, conditional probability

Bayes’ Theorem in ML (e.g., Naive Bayes)


Stage 3: Data Handling & Visualization

Data Preprocessing:

Handling null values (drop, impute)

Removing duplicates

Detecting & handling outliers (Z-score, IQR)

Data transformation: encoding (OneHot, Label), scaling (Standard, MinMax)


Feature Engineering:

Feature extraction and selection

Creating new features from existing data

Feature importance (based on models)


Exploratory Data Analysis (EDA):

Understanding distributions, relationships

Correlation heatmaps

GroupBy, aggregation, pivot tables

Trend analysis, time-based grouping


Visualization:

Seaborn (pairplot, boxplot, heatmap, violinplot)

Matplotlib (line, bar, pie, scatter)

Plotly (interactive visualizations)


Stage 4: Core Machine Learning

1. Supervised Learning
Regression:

Linear Regression

Ridge & Lasso Regression

Polynomial Regression


Classification:

Logistic Regression

K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN)

Support Vector Machines (SVM)

Decision Trees

Random Forest

Gradient Boosting, XGBoost, LightGBM


Ensemble Learning:

Bagging vs Boosting

Voting Classifier

Stacking Models


Hyperparameter Tuning:

GridSearchCV, RandomizedSearchCV

Parameter tuning for different models


Imbalanced Datasets:

SMOTE, undersampling, oversampling

Using class weights


2. Unsupervised Learning
K-Means Clustering

Hierarchical Clustering

DBSCAN

Principal Component Analysis (PCA)

t-SNE and UMAP for visualization


3. Model Evaluation
Metrics:

Regression: MAE, MSE, RMSE, R²

Classification: Accuracy, Precision, Recall, F1-score, ROC-AUC

Confusion Matrix


Techniques:

Cross-validation (K-Fold, Stratified)

Train-test split

Overfitting vs Underfitting

Bias-variance tradeoff


Model Interpretability:

SHAP values

LIME

Feature importance (based on trees or coefficients)


Stage 5: Advanced Topics
1. Feature Engineering & Selection
Recursive Feature Elimination (RFE)

SelectKBest, mutual information

Feature scaling and normalization


2. Time Series Analysis
Stationarity, trend, seasonality

Autocorrelation, Partial Autocorrelation

ARIMA, SARIMA

LSTM basics for time series


3. Natural Language Processing (NLP)
Text cleaning (lowercasing, stopword removal, stemming, lemmatization)

Tokenization

Vectorization (Bag of Words, TF-IDF, Word2Vec)

Sentiment analysis

Intro to transformers, Hugging Face, and BERT


4. Deep Learning
Neural Networks: perceptrons, forward/backpropagation

CNNs: image data

RNNs, LSTMs: sequential/time-series data

Libraries: TensorFlow, Keras, PyTorch (basics)


5. Prompt Engineering (for LLMs)
Basic prompt structuring

Few-shot examples

Role prompting

Token limitations


Stage 6: Real-World Projects & Deployment
Capstone Projects:

Kaggle competitions

UCI datasets

Personal projects with GitHub repo + README + notebook

Deployment:

Flask or FastAPI to serve ML models

Docker: containerize ML apps

Cloud: Deploy on AWS, GCP, or Azure (free tiers)

Streamlit or Gradio for fast UI demos

Experiment Tracking & Versioning:

MLflow

Weights & Biases

DVC (Data Version Control)

Testing & Monitoring:

API testing with Postman

CI/CD basics

Monitoring models in production (conceptual)
